title: Count all rows
prompt: Show how many employees there are, as total. Replace the ___.
starterSql:
SELECT COUNT(___) AS total
FROM employees;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(bonus) AS total FROM employees;

title: Count known values
prompt: Show how many employees have a recorded email, as with_email.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT COUNT(email) AS with_email FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS with_email FROM employees;
SELECT COUNT(bonus) AS with_email FROM employees;

title: Count different values
prompt: Show how many different cities customers live in, as cities.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) AS cities FROM customers;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(city) AS cities FROM customers;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS cities FROM customers;

title: Graded enrolments
prompt: Show the number of enrolments as total, and the number with a grade as graded.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(grade) AS graded FROM enrolments;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(*) AS graded FROM enrolments;
SELECT COUNT(grade) AS total, COUNT(grade) AS graded FROM enrolments;

title: Counting nothing
prompt: Show how many orders have the status lost, as lost_orders. None do, and the answer should be 0, not an empty result.
hints: COUNT returns 0 when no rows match.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE orders SET status = 'lost' WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS lost_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'lost';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id AS lost_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'lost';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS lost_orders FROM orders;

title: Fix the distinct count
prompt: This should show how many different users have sessions, as active_users, but it fails. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT DISTINCT COUNT user_id AS active_users
FROM sessions;
solutions: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS active_users FROM sessions;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(user_id) AS active_users FROM sessions;
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS active_users FROM sessions;

title: Missing rain
prompt: Show how many readings have no rainfall recorded, as missing, by subtracting one count from another.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM readings; INSERT INTO readings VALUES (11, 'Cairo', '2024-07-30', 38, 0.0), (12, 'Cairo', '2024-07-31', 40, NULL), (13, 'Cairo', '2024-08-01', 41, 0.5), (14, 'Quito', '2024-07-31', 15, 3.0), (15, 'Quito', '2024-08-01', 14, 3.0), (16, 'Quito', '2024-08-03', 18, NULL); UPDATE readings SET rainfall_mm = NULL WHERE id = 11;

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(rainfall_mm) AS missing FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(rainfall_mm) AS missing FROM readings;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS missing FROM readings;

title: Customers who ordered in March
prompt: Show how many different customers placed an order in March 2024, as march_customers.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE orders SET order_date = '2024-03-31', customer_id = 8 WHERE id = 13; INSERT INTO orders VALUES (14, 8, '2024-03-05', 'shipped');

solutions: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS march_customers FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-03-01' AND '2024-03-31';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(customer_id) AS march_customers FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-03-01' AND '2024-03-31';
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS march_customers FROM orders;
